newsitem.title: UK: Energy Group to pay 5.5 p/shr final dividend.
newsitem.headline: Energy Group to pay 5.5 p/shr final dividend.

text.p: The Energy Group, spun off from Hanson Plc on Monday, said it would change its year-end to March 31 and added it expected to pay a final dividend of 5.5 pence per share for the three months to March 31, 1997.
The dividend, to be paid in August 1997, represents one quarter of the dividend the directors expect would have been paid had the company been listed for a full calendar year, the Energy Group said.
The group earlier reported that its operating profit for the three months to December 31 rose 138 million stg from 100 million stg.
Executive chairman Derek Bonham said the Energy Group had demonstrated the strength of its core operations, which would provide an excellent base for future expansion.
"The Energy Group has an enviable position across the power industry and we are confident that 1997 will prove a period of real progress," said Bonham.

The Energy Group said its coal operating profits remained unchnaged at 25 million stg. Coal prices in the eastern and midwestern U.S. coal fields firmed, but revenues fell to 325 million stg from 329 million as prices eased in the Powder River Bassin.
Operating profit from the power business climbed to 57 million stg from 23 million.
Revenues rose to 759 million stg from 501 million following a strong contribution new electricity generating operations.
Since July, Energy Group's electricity arm Eastern controls 5,900 MW of coal-fired capacity via operating leases from National Power and PowerGen.
In the UK domestic gas market, which is seeing the gradual dismantling of British Gas' monopoly, Eastern has won 40,000 customers. The number continues to grow, the Energy Group said.
